Synthetic account shows billed usage rose from 640 kWh (June) to 870 kWh (July) with actual meter reads of 41820 kWh (2026-06-30) and 42690 kWh (2026-07-31); a remote self-test on 2026-07-29 passed with no tamper or register fault flags. Material allegations: meter malfunction caused increased charge. Investigation steps: (1) verify meter read sequence and billing calculation for July 2026; (2) review diagnostics and tamper/event logs (already shows remote test PASS); (3) request/obtain on-site meter accuracy test or field inspection if diagnostics are inconclusive; (4) perform usage analysis vs prior months/seasonal baseline and check for rate or service changes; (5) collect customer information about behavioral/household changes during the period; (6) escalate to meter operations for field test if on-site evidence missing or results abnormal; (7) document findings and determine next procedural actions per policy."
}

We reviewed your July 2026 bill because you reported a large increase and asked whether the meter caused it. Based on the records we have, the meter register readings and the billed kWh match, and a recent remote diagnostic test showed no tamper or register-fault flags. At this time we cannot confirm the meter is broken; an on-site field test is required to confirm or rule out a meter fault. Any billing adjustment must be authorized by a human billing supervisor after that test if a fault is found.

What we reviewed
We reviewed your account billing records for June and July 2026, the meter register reads on 2026-06-30 and 2026-07-31, the posted billed amounts for both months, the supplied rate components (energy charge and fixed charge), the remote diagnostic self-test performed 2026-07-29, and the meter event log covering the period.

What we found
The difference between the meter register on 2026-07-31 and 2026-06-30 equals 870 kWh, which matches the billed July usage. Applying the supplied rate components to that usage produces the billed amount shown on your July bill. The remote self-test on 2026-07-29 returned PASS with no tamper or register fault flags, and no meter events were recorded in the interval. We do not see any arithmetic or rate-application error in the supplied records.

Why your bill changed
The records show your measured consumption increased from 640 kWh in June to 870 kWh in July (an increase of 230 kWh). The billed amount increased accordingly because the meter register difference and the billing calculation match the higher usage. The supplied diagnostics do not show a meter fault, so the available evidence supports that the bill change is due to higher measured usage rather than a documented billing error or a remote-detected meter malfunction.

What happens next
Because remote diagnostics cannot rule out all possible meter issues, the next step is a field inspection and on-site meter accuracy test. We will request a field test from Meter Operations; that test report will determine whether the meter is within tolerance. If the on-site test shows a verified meter fault or register error, we will prepare an adjustment request and escalate it to a human Billing Supervisor for approval. If the on-site test shows the meter is functioning properly, no automatic adjustment will be made and we will close the investigation after documenting findings. We will keep you updated on scheduling and results.

What we need from you
Please let us know whether there were any changes in your household or equipment in July 2026 (for example: occupants, new appliances, HVAC or EV charging patterns) that could explain higher usage. Also confirm whether you can provide access for a field technician to perform an on-site meter test at a mutually convenient time. No further action on billing will be taken until the on-site test is completed and reviewed by a human supervisor if a fault is found.
